title: Characteristic ideal of the fine Selmer group and results on $Œº$-invariance under isogeny in the function field case

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper begins with an arbitrary one-variable function field K over a finite field, but then defines its curve as "C_K = P^1_F". A general global function field is the function field of an arbitrary smooth projective curve, not necessarily P^1. This unjustified specialization conflicts with later claims stated for general function fields.

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.4, definition and properties of the functor G
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The displayed definition reads "G := lim_n ((X/omega_n X)[p^infty])" rather than defining G(X), and then states "Phi_0 = X". Phi_0 must be an element of Lambda (normally omega_0=T), whereas X is a module. Thus the definitions used subsequently, including products involving Phi_0, are not mathematically well-formed.

The manuscript repeatedly invokes "Lemma 2.9" (for example, "applying Lemma 2.9(iii)" in Proposition 3.5), but no Lemma 2.9 is stated anywhere. The missing lemma is essential to the asserted exactness after passing to maximal divisible subgroups, so the proof cannot be checked as written.

Both displayed bounds are stated for H^1(G,B): "|H^1(G,B)| <= |B|^d" and again "|H^1(G,B)| <= |B|^{d(d-1)/2}". The standard result cited from Bandini--Longhi gives the second bound for H^2(G,B), not H^1. As written the second statement is generally false and misquotes the cited lemma.

The proof asserts "0 = (A(L_n) tensor Q_p/Z_p)_div". This is false whenever A(L_n) has positive Mordell--Weil rank: A(L_n) tensor Q_p/Z_p contains (Q_p/Z_p)^{rank A(L_n)}, which is divisible. Therefore the short exact sequence of divisible parts used to prove G((A(L_infty) tensor Q_p/Z_p)^vee)=0 is invalid.

The control map defined in the proposition is m_n: M^S(E/L_n) -> M^S(E/L_infty)^{Gamma_n}, induced by inclusion. The diagrams instead draw the vertical maps downward from the infinite-level invariant groups to finite-level groups and call them f_n/m_n. There is no natural restriction/control morphism in that displayed direction. Consequently the snake-lemma arguments concern maps that have not been defined.

The proposition has only a stated part (a), but its proof repeatedly says "To prove (a) and (b)" and concludes "Then, (b) follows". No part (b) exists. In particular, the claimed cokernel conclusion is not part of a formulated proposition and cannot support later uses as a control theorem.

The formula defining e_n uses rank E(L_{n-1}) and is explicitly given only for n >= 1, but the main characteristic-ideal formulas take products over n >= 0 and use e_0. Neither L_{-1} nor e_0 is defined. Since Phi_0 was also incorrectly defined as X in Section 2.4, the n=0 factor in the principal result is undefined.

The conclusion is written "Char_Lambda(M^S(E/L_infty))^vee", i.e. the Pontryagin dual of a characteristic ideal, rather than Char_Lambda(M^S(E/L_infty)^vee). A characteristic ideal is an ideal, not a discrete module to which the displayed dual operation is defined. This differs from the correctly typed target in Theorem 4.9.

Immediately after stating Theorem 4.9, its "Proof" starts with diagrams involving two isogenous curves E_1,E_2, maps lambda_i, and classical Selmer groups; these are unrelated to the fine-Mordell--Weil argument of Theorem 4.9 and are the material for Theorem 5.1. No proof of the stated characteristic-ideal equality is provided. Moreover, its finiteness assumption is written "S^S(E/L_infty) is finite", although the defined fine Tate--Shafarevich group is mathfrak X^S, so the hypothesis itself is undefined.

Theorem 1.6 assumes H^2_fl(K_infty,E_i[p^infty])=0. Theorem 5.1, claimed to be that theorem, instead assumes H^1_fl(K_infty,E_i[p^infty])=0. Its proof repeatedly uses the H^2-vanishing assumption, e.g. "The assumption H^2_fl(K_infty,E_1[p^infty])=0 implies...". Thus the proof does not establish the theorem as stated, and the main-result statement contradicts the introduction.

predicted_errors.error_location: Proof of Theorem 5.1, discussion of f_4 after equation (10)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof says "Gal(K_{infty,w}/K_{infty,w}) is isomorphic to product_{ell != p} Z_ell" and concludes ker(f_4)=coker(f_4)=0. The displayed Galois group is of a field over itself and is therefore trivial; it cannot be the claimed product. If K_v was intended, the claimed group is still not the decomposition group of the unramified Z_p-extension. This invalidates the local-term vanishing needed for the proof.

The remark states that "the order of the kernel of isogeny equals its separable degree" and therefore a purely inseparable Frobenius isogeny has trivial kernel for the argument. For an isogeny in characteristic p, the kernel is a finite flat group scheme whose rank equals the full degree, not merely the separable degree. The Frobenius kernel is a nontrivial connected finite group scheme (despite possibly having only the identity geometric point), which is especially relevant because the paper uses flat cohomology.

K_infty is defined as the l-power torsion/trivializing extension K(E[l^infty]), whose Galois group is stated earlier to be an open subgroup of GL_2(Z_l). Theorems 1.5 and 6.3 additionally assume this G is "pro-p" for p != l. A nontrivial open subgroup of GL_2(Z_l) contains an open pro-l congruence subgroup and cannot be pro-p when p != l. Hence the announced hypothesis is incompatible with the defined trivializing extension (apart from degenerate cases not covered by the claims).

predicted_errors.error_location: Definition 2.14 and Sections 6 and Appendix A
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Definition 2.14 defines mu using p-primary layers p^i(M[p^infty])/p^{i+1}. In the l != p portions, the relevant Iwasawa algebra and Selmer module are Z_l- and l-primary, but the proofs continue to cite this definition and use ord_p and p-power annihilation (for example Appendix A: "mu(M)=ord_p(...)" and "annihilated by a power of p"). The relevant invariant would have to be defined with l, not p. Thus the stated mu computations in the l-adic setting do not follow from the supplied definitions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A, diagram (13) and proof of Theorem A.1
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Diagram (13) labels the Selmer terms S(E_i/K), while its middle cohomology terms are over G_S(mathcal K) and the theorem concerns S(E_i/mathcal K). The proof then alternates between g_i and f_i, refers to an unlabelled "equation (A)", and uses K_infty in the Case 1 calculation for K_cyc. These are not merely cosmetic: they leave the maps whose kernels and cokernels are calculated unidentified, so the snake-lemma and Euler-characteristic argument is not a valid proof of Theorem A.1.
